sources.title: United States Counterterrorism Strategy 2026
bounded_observations: Lists 'Violent Left-Wing Extremists, including Anarchists and Anti-Fascists' as one of three major types of terror groups.
States CT powers will not be used against Americans who simply disagree with the administration.
Directs prioritization of violent secular political groups and describes mapping membership and ties to international organizations like Antifa.
States CT mission is to identify groups with intent and capability to plot attacks against Americans and neutralize them.

sources.title: Designating Antifa as a Domestic Terrorist Organization
bounded_observations: Designates Antifa as a domestic terrorist organization by executive order.
Directs agencies to investigate, disrupt, and dismantle illegal operations conducted by Antifa or persons claiming to act on its behalf, including material-support investigations.

sources.title: Countering Domestic Terrorism and Organized Political Violence (NSPM-7)
bounded_observations: Directs JTTFs to coordinate a national strategy to investigate, prosecute, and disrupt entities and individuals engaged in political violence and intimidation.
Extends investigative attention to recruitment/radicalization, funders, organizations, and networks.
Allows the Attorney General to recommend domestic-terrorist-organization designation for groups whose members engage in activities meeting 18 U.S.C. §2331(5).

sources.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2331 — Definitions
bounded_observations: Domestic terrorism requires acts dangerous to human life that violate criminal law, specified coercive/governmental intent, and primarily domestic occurrence.

sources.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2339A — Providing material support to terrorists
bounded_observations: Applies when material support or resources are provided knowing or intending they be used in preparation for or carrying out enumerated federal crimes.
Defines material support broadly to include property, services, training, communications equipment, personnel, and transportation.
Does not itself require that the recipient be a State Department-designated foreign terrorist organization.

sources.title: Antifa Cell Members Convicted in Prairieland ICE Detention Center Shooting
sources.organization: U.S. Department of Justice / Northern District of Texas
bounded_observations: Reports jury convictions for riot, providing material support to terrorists, explosive offenses, attempted murder, and obstruction-related counts depending on defendant.
States some defendants attended a peaceful daytime protest before later conduct alleged and proved at trial.
Reports seven additional defendants pleaded guilty to a single material-support count.
limitations: Press release is the government's characterization, not a substitute for charging documents, factual resumes, jury instructions, or judgments.

sources.title: Leader of Antifa Cell Members in North Texas Sentenced to 100 Years in Prison for Terrorist Attack on ICE Facility
bounded_observations: Describes the alleged/established cell as part of a larger militant enterprise composed of networks of individuals and small groups primarily ascribing to an ideology.
Again states some defendants attended a peaceful daytime protest and reported security details.
Reports sentences and material-support convictions/pleas tied to a broader violent event.
limitations: Does not establish that peaceful protest alone supplied the statutory predicate for any defendant.

sources.title: 5 Prairieland ICE shooting defendants plead guilty to federal terrorism-related charge
bounded_observations: Reports defense counsel's characterization that one defendant admitted property damage but denied violent intent.
Reports differing conduct allegations among defendants, reinforcing need for defendant-level analysis.

sources.title: Ninth Prairieland defendant sentenced; six who pleaded guilty receive prison terms
bounded_observations: Reports distinct factual roles among plea defendants, including presence at Prairieland, property damage, and post-event assistance to the alleged shooter.
Reports appeals had begun in the Fifth Circuit after district-court proceedings.
